article_context: 粉色、性别编码与儿童营销。语气带反思感，强调所谓“自然偏好”背后的商业塑造。

article.title: 阅读二 · 粉色如何被塑造成“女孩色”
article.background: 粉色、性别编码与儿童营销。语气带反思感，强调所谓“自然偏好”背后的商业塑造。

sentences.en: Pretty in pink: adult women do not remember being so obsessed with the colour, yet it is pervasive in our young girls’ lives.
sentences.zh: “粉红真漂亮”：成年的女性并不记得自己小时候曾如此迷恋这种颜色，可如今粉红色却几乎充斥着小女孩的生活。

vocab.meaning: a. 着迷的；无法摆脱的

segments.text: Pretty in pink: adult women do not remember being so obsessed with the colour, yet it is pervasive in our young girls’ lives.

sentences.en: It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls’ identity to appearance.
sentences.zh: 问题并不是粉红色本身有什么不好，而是它只是彩虹中极小的一部分；它也许以某种方式赞美了女孩时代，却又不断而坚定地把女孩的身份与外表绑在一起。

segments.text: It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls’ identity to appearance.

sentences.en: Then it presents that connection, even among two-year-olds, between girls as not only innocent but as evidence of innocence.
sentences.zh: 更进一步，这种关联甚至从两岁左右就被呈现为不仅天真无害，而且仿佛还是“天真”的证据。

segments.text: Then it presents that connection, even among two-year-olds, between girls as not only innocent but as evidence of innocence.

sentences.en: Looking around, I despaired at the singular lack of imagination about girls’ lives and interests.
sentences.zh: 环顾四周，我对人们想象女孩生活和兴趣时如此单一贫乏感到失望。

segments.text: Looking around, I despaired at the singular lack of imagination about girls’ lives and interests.

sentences.en: Girls’ attraction to pink may seem unavoidable, somehow encoded in their DNA, but according to Jo Paoletti, an associate professor of American Studies, it is not.
sentences.zh: 女孩对粉红色的偏爱似乎不可避免，仿佛写进了DNA，但美国研究副教授乔·保莱蒂认为事实并非如此。

vocab.meaning: a. 不可避免的；不得已的

segments.text: Girls’ attraction to pink may seem unavoidable, somehow encoded in their DNA, but according to Jo Paoletti, an associate professor of American Studies, it is not.

sentences.en: Children were not colour-coded at all until the early 20th century: in the era before domestic washing machines all babies wore white as a practical matter, since the only way of getting clothes clean was to boil them.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪初，儿童根本没有按颜色区分性别。在没有家用洗衣机的年代，为了实用，所有婴儿都穿白色衣服，因为只有煮洗才能把衣服洗干净。

segments.text: Children were not colour-coded at all until the early 20th century: in the era before domestic washing machines all babies wore white as a practical matter, since the only way of getting clothes clean was to boil them.

sentences.en: What’s more, both boys and girls wore what were thought of as gender-neutral dresses.
sentences.zh: 更何况，当时男孩和女孩穿的都是被视为性别中性的裙装。

segments.text: What’s more, both boys and girls wore what were thought of as gender-neutral dresses.

sentences.en: When nursery colours were introduced, pink was actually considered the more masculine colour, a pastel version of red, which was associated with strength.
sentences.zh: 托儿室颜色出现后，粉红色反而被看作更男性化的颜色——它是红色的浅色版本，而红色与力量相联系。

segments.text: When nursery colours were introduced, pink was actually considered the more masculine colour, a pastel version of red, which was associated with strength.

sentences.en: Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised femininity.
sentences.zh: 蓝色由于让人联想到圣母玛利亚、忠贞与信仰，反而象征女性气质。

segments.text: Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised femininity.

sentences.en: It was not until the mid-1980s, when amplifying age and sex differences became a dominant children’s marketing strategy, that pink fully came into its own, when it began to seem inherently attractive to girls, part of what defined them as female, at least for the first few critical years.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪80年代中期，放大年龄和性别差异成为儿童营销的主导策略，粉红色才真正“属于”女孩：它开始显得天生就对女孩有吸引力，仿佛成为界定女性身份的一部分，至少在人生最初几个关键年份如此。

segments.text: It was not until the mid-1980s, when amplifying age and sex differences became a dominant children’s marketing strategy, that pink fully came into its own, when it began to seem inherently attractive to girls, part of what defined them as female, at least for the first few critical years.

sentences.en: I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development.
sentences.zh: 我此前从未意识到，营销趋势竟如此深刻地支配着我们对“儿童天性”的认识，甚至影响我们对儿童心理发展的核心信念。

vocab.meaning: a. 心理学的；精神上的

segments.text: I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development.

sentences.en: I assumed that phase was something experts developed after years of research into children’s behaviour: wrong.
sentences.zh: 我原以为这个阶段是专家经过多年儿童行为研究后划分出来的；事实并非如此。

segments.text: I assumed that phase was something experts developed after years of research into children’s behaviour: wrong.

sentences.en: Turns out, according to Daniel Cook, a historian of childhood consumerism, it was popularised as a marketing trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 儿童消费史学者丹尼尔·库克指出，“toddler（幼儿）”其实是20世纪30年代服装制造商作为营销技巧推广开的。

segments.text: Turns out, according to Daniel Cook, a historian of childhood consumerism, it was popularised as a marketing trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s.

sentences.en: Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should create a “third stepping stone” between infant wear and older kids’ clothes.
sentences.zh: 行业刊物建议百货商店，为了增加销售额，应在婴儿服装和大孩子服装之间人为创造“第三块踏脚石”。

segments.text: Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should create a “third stepping stone” between infant wear and older kids’ clothes.

sentences.en: It was only after “toddler” became a common shoppers’ term that it evolved into a broadly accepted developmental stage.
sentences.zh: 直到“toddler”成为购物者的常用词，它才逐渐演变为一个广泛接受的发展阶段。

segments.text: It was only after “toddler” became a common shoppers’ term that it evolved into a broadly accepted developmental stage.

sentences.en: Splitting kids, or adults, into ever-tinier categories has proved a sure-fire way to boost profits.
sentences.zh: 把儿童或成年人切分成越来越细小的类别，已经被证明是一种可靠的增利手段。

segments.text: Splitting kids, or adults, into ever-tinier categories has proved a sure-fire way to boost profits.

sentences.en: And one of the easiest ways to segment a market is to magnify gender differences – or invent them where they did not previously exist.
sentences.zh: 而细分市场最容易的方法之一，就是放大性别差异——或者在原本不存在差异的地方发明差异。

segments.text: And one of the easiest ways to segment a market is to magnify gender differences – or invent them where they did not previously exist.
